source: Order adapted from the Daily Turkish deck: each lemma of its ranked list (itself adapted from the 2018 Turkish list of FrequencyWords by Hermit Dave, CC BY-SA 4.0, built from the OpenSubtitles2018 corpus) was matched by meaning to its usual Turkmen equivalent, then edited by hand: film-dialogue words dropped or moved down, Turkish lemmas that share one Turkmen word merged, everyday Turkmen words added where their use would put them. Ranks are an editorial estimate, not a Turkmen corpus count. The ranked list is scripts/turkmen/tm-wordlist.tsv (CC BY-SA 4.0); method in turkmen/TM-PROJECT.md 7.8. Glosses, examples and notes are original.

ex.en: My father is a teacher at a school.
My older sister is a university student.

cards.note: p becomes b before a vowel: *talyby*, *talybym*. A schoolchild is an *okuwçy*.
*Söz bermek* (to promise, literally to give your word).

ex.en: I have some good news for you.

cards.note: *Habar bermek* (to let someone know).
The other one of a known set. For **another, a different one**, use *başga*.

ex.en: She wrote a letter to her friend.
The food's ready, come and eat!

cards.note: *Nahar iýmek* (to have a meal), *nahar bişirmek* (to cook).
Before *bir*, **one more, another**: *ýene bir gün* (one more day).
Doing something over from the start. The everyday **again** is *ýene*.
From *okamak* (to read, to study), like *okuwçy* (pupil).
The person you apologize to takes *-dan*: *senden ötünç soraýaryn*. The everyday **sorry** is *bagyşlaň*.
Also **to turn on**: *telewizory açmak* (to turn on the TV).

ex.en: My father took me to school.

cards.note: t becomes d before a vowel and before *-ýär*: *äkidýär*, *äkider*. Bringing something here is *getirmek*.

ex.en: I have three younger brothers and sisters.

cards.note: Its vowel is long. *Üçünji* (third).

ex.en: The school is on the right.

cards.note: *Sagda* (on the right), *saga* (to the right). Also **healthy**: *sag bol* (thank you) is literally **be healthy**.

ex.en: Take your book out of the bag.

cards.note: From *çykmak* (to go out): literally **to make go out**.

ex.en: In my opinion, this book is interesting.

cards.note: Takes the dative: *maňa görä* (in my opinion), *meýilnama görä* (according to plan).

ex.en: Cut the bread with a knife.

cards.note: Not *bilen* (with): *Men Merdan bilen geldim* (I came with Merdan), but *Biz bile geldik* (We came together).
The direction **in**. Opposite: *daşary* (outside).
Takes a negative verb: *Ol hiç haçan gijä galmaýar* (He's never late).

ex.en: Please sit down and have some tea.

cards.note: *Otyr* (is sitting) also builds a progressive after a verb in *-yp*: *okap otyr* (is reading).
Something changing by itself. To change something is *üýtgetmek*.
*Taýýarlamak* (to prepare).
The direction **out**. *Daşary ýurt* (abroad, a foreign country). Opposite: *içeri* (inside).

ex.en: Hurry up, or we'll be late.
The men are drinking tea in the teahouse.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *erkegi*. Also before a noun: *erkek kişi* (a man).

ex.en: The old man is sitting in the teahouse.

cards.note: A respectful word for an older man, from *ýaş* (age) and *uly* (big, old).
*Pikir etmek* (to think). *Meniň pikirimçe* (in my opinion).
From *geçmek* (to pass): literally **to make pass**. *Toý geçirmek* (to hold a wedding).
The u drops before a vowel: *oglum* (my son), *ogly* (his son). **Boy** is *oglan*.
k becomes g before a vowel: *bäbegi*.
Of people, **tall**: *uzyn adam*. Opposite: *gysga*.
Something getting lost by itself is *ýitmek*: *Açarym ýitdi* (My key has gone missing).
Mostly in set phrases: *Hoş geldiňiz!* (Welcome!), *Hoş gal!* (Goodbye!).

ex.en: The boy hit the ball against the wall.

cards.note: What something hits takes the dative: *diwara urmak*.
*Baş* also means **head**, and **beginning** too.
As a noun, **sweets**: *süýji iýmek* (to eat sweets).
*Jan saglygy* (health). After a name, *-jan* makes it affectionate: *Aýnajan*, *Merdanjan*.

ex.en: I stayed in Ashgabat for a few days.

cards.note: The noun after it stays singular: *birnäçe gün*.

ex.en: I bought a kilo of apples at the market.

cards.note: What you fear takes *-dan*: *itden gorkmak*.

ex.en: My room is small but bright.

cards.note: *Myhman otagy* (guest room, living room).
From *soramak* (to ask).

ex.en: I have to go to the doctor.

cards.note: To call someone is *jaň etmek*.
*Gaty* means the same.
Also **loudly**: *Gaty gürleme* (Don't talk so loudly). As an adjective, **hard**: *gaty ýer* (hard ground).

ex.en: The cat ran away from the dog.

cards.note: What you run from takes *-dan*.

ex.en: Something interesting happened in the street yesterday.

cards.note: *Ses bermek* (to vote).

ex.en: He earns a lot of money.
There's a big carpet in the middle of the room.

cards.note: *-yň ortasynda* (in the middle of). As an adjective: *orta mekdep* (secondary school).
*Geçen hepde* (last week), *indiki hepde* (next week).

ex.en: She put on a white dress.

cards.note: *Ak öý* (the white felt yurt), *Ak ýol!* (Have a good trip!).
Also **dark**: *gara saç* (dark hair).
As a noun, **gold**: *gyzyl ýüzük* (a gold ring).
Also **green** for plants and tea: *gök çaý* (green tea). For other green things, *ýaşyl*.

ex.en: There are lots of green trees in the park.
The inside of the melon is yellow.
The children are playing football in the street.

cards.note: For a musical instrument, *çalmak*: *dutar çalmak*.
Optional after a number, mostly with things: *üç sany kitap* or *üç kitap*. For people, *kişi*.
Takes the dative: *maňa degişli* (mine, belonging to me).
Another verb before it takes *-maga/-mäge*: *gelmäge synanyşdy* (he tried to come).

ex.en: My father has an old car.

cards.note: For people, **old** is *garry*.

ex.en: My grandfather lives in the village.

cards.note: Its dative is *oba* too: *oba gitmek* (to go to the village).

ex.en: The cat is under the chair.

cards.note: *-yň aşagynda* (under). Also **down**: *aşak düş* (come down). k becomes g before a vowel.
*Bagtly* (happy) is built on it.
Its p stays before a vowel: *tarapy*, *tarapyndan* (by).
The *dutar* is the two-stringed Turkmen lute. For games and sports, *oýnamak*.
*Ýigrimi ýaşymda* (at twenty). Not the adjective *ýaş* (young).
Not the noun *ýaş* (age). *Ýaşlar* (young people).

ex.en: I'd like to drink some water.

cards.note: *Etli* (with meat): *etli çörek* (bread with meat).
*-yň arkasynda* (behind).
Who it goes to takes the dative: *saňa iberdim*.

ex.en: I spent a month in Mary.

cards.note: Also **the moon**. *Geçen aý* (last month), *her aý* (every month).

ex.en: Some people drink coffee in the morning.

cards.note: The noun after it is usually plural: *käbir adamlar*.
*Akylly* (clever) is built on it.
*Karar kabul etmek* (to make a decision).

ex.en: How many manat is this book?

cards.note: No *-my* with it: *Sagat näçe?* (What time is it?). The noun after it stays singular: *näçe kitap?*

ex.en: I wanted to, but I didn't have time.

cards.note: Means the same as *ýöne*, a little more formal.

ex.en: My older sister studies in Ashgabat.

cards.note: A younger brother or sister is a *jigi*.

ex.en: My little brother goes to school.

cards.note: An older sister is an *uýa*, an older brother an *aga*.
Who you agree with takes *bilen*: *seniň bilen ylalaşýaryn*.

en: to get to know, to meet (for the first time)
cards.note: *Tanyşanyma şat* (pleased to meet you). The person takes *bilen*: *onuň bilen tanyşdym*.

ex.en: We watched TV in the evening.

cards.note: What you watch takes the dative: *filme tomaşa etmek*.

ex.en: Everyone at the wedding is happy.

cards.note: From *bagt* (happiness).
*Zähmet haky* (wages). *Hakly* (right, entitled): *Sen hakly* (You're right).

en: to get off (a bus, a train)

ex.en: The book fell off the table.

cards.note: Where from takes *-dan*: *awtobusdan düşmek* (to get off the bus).
To **be late** for something is *gijä galmak*.

ex.en: In winter it's cold in Dashoguz.

cards.note: *Sowuk suw* (cold water). Opposite: *gyzgyn* (hot), and for the weather *yssy*.

ex.en: In summer it's very hot in Ashgabat.

cards.note: For hot things, *gyzgyn*: *gyzgyn çaý* (hot tea).
ç becomes j before a vowel: *güýji*, *güýjüm*. *Güýçli* (strong).

ex.en: My grandfather made a toy out of wood.

cards.note: Making with your hands. Cooking is *bişirmek*.
*Hökman däl* (not necessary).

ex.en: There's a long queue at the shop.
I'll be at home this evening.

cards.note: On its own it also means **in the evening**: *Agşam gel* (come in the evening). *Agşamyňyz haýyrly bolsun* (good evening).

ex.en: My grandfather goes to the park every day.

cards.note: **Grandmother** is *ene*.

ex.en: I read the newspaper every day.

cards.note: Also **to study**: *Ol uniwersitetde okaýar* (She's at university).

ex.en: Our school is big and new.

cards.note: p becomes b before a vowel: *mekdebe* (to school), *mekdebim* (my school); but *mekdepde* (at school).
The u drops before a vowel: *urşy*, *urşunda* (in the war).
Also **morning**: *ertirlik* (breakfast).

ex.en: I get up at seven in the morning.

cards.note: *Ir* (early): *ir turmak* (to get up early).

ex.en: We reached Mary in the evening.

cards.note: Also **to be enough**: *Pul ýetmeýär* (There isn't enough money). *Ýeter!* (That's enough!).

ex.tk: Umyt edýärin, ertir howa gowy bolar.
ex.en: I hope the weather will be good tomorrow.

cards.note: *Umyt* (hope) voices its t before a vowel: *umydym* (my hope).

ex.en: Attention, please: the lesson is starting.

cards.note: *Üns bermek* (to pay attention) takes the dative: *maňa üns beriň*.
The u drops before a vowel: *oýny*, *oýnuň*. *Oýnamak* (to play) is built on it.

ex.en: The shop is open until nine.

cards.note: Also **light** for colours: *açyk gök* (light blue). Opposite: *ýapyk* (closed).

ex.tk: Men her gün işe ýöräp gidýärin.
ex.en: I walk to work every day.

cards.note: The e of the stem becomes ä before *-p* and *-r*: *ýöräp*, *ýörär*.
*Bagyşlaň!* (Excuse me! Sorry!) is its polite imperative; to someone you call *sen*, *bagyşla*.
*Nirede* (where), *nirä* (where to).
*Ýalňyşmak* (to make a mistake), *ýalňyşlyk* (a mistake).
*Ärim* (my husband). **Wife** is *aýal*.
*Sürüji* (driver) is built on it.
*Bir gezek* (once), *ilkinji gezek* (the first time). k becomes g before a vowel: *gezegi*.
The e of the stem becomes ä before *-p* and *-r*: *töläp*, *tölär*.
Always written with a hyphen. A little more formal than *we*.

ex.en: We parted at the bus stop.

cards.note: Who you part from takes *-dan*: *dostundan aýryldy*.
*Ýalan sözlemek* (to lie). Opposite: *dogry* (true).

ex.en: I had yogurt and bread in the morning.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *gatygy*.

ex.en: The child threw a stone into the water.

cards.note: Its vowel is long, unlike *daş* (far, outside), as in *daşary* (outside).
*Aýratyn hem* (especially).
Also a canteen: *mekdebiň aşhanasy* (the school canteen).
*Haýsysy?* (Which one?).

ex.en: The guests have gone, I'm alone at home.
The yard is roomy and clean.

cards.note: From *söýmek* (to love).

ex.en: The school is far from our house.

cards.note: What it's far from takes *-dan*. *Uzak wagt* (a long time). Opposite: *ýakyn*.

ex.en: The children drink milk every day.
We live in the city, my grandfather in the village.
Give me a piece of bread.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *bölegi*.

ex.en: There are no classes in the afternoon.
I get up early every day.

cards.note: *Ir turmak* (to get up early). *Turuň!* (Stand up!).

ex.en: We saw a new film in the evening.

cards.note: Takes *-dan*: *irden bäri* (since the morning), *köp ýyldan bäri* (for many years).
What you're interested in takes *bilen*: *saz bilen gyzyklanmak*. *Gyzykly* (interesting).
Its vowel is long, so t becomes d before a vowel: *ody*, *oda*. Not *ot* (grass), with a short vowel: *oty*.

ex.en: The weather will be rainy tomorrow.

cards.note: Also **air**: *arassa howa* (fresh air).
*Öňňin* (the day before yesterday).

ex.en: The doctor listened to my heart.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *ýüregim*, *ýüregi*.
*Kitap* (book) and *-hana* (place, house), as in *çaýhana* and *hassahana*.

ex.en: No reply came to my letter.

cards.note: p becomes b before a vowel: *jogaby*. *Jogap bermek* (to answer).

ex.en: The child has already fallen asleep.

cards.note: Going to bed is *ýatmak*; sleeping is *uklamak*.
*Ýagyş ýagýar* (it's raining). *Ýagyşly* (rainy).
Takes the dative. The e of the stem becomes ä before *-p* and *-r*: *meňzäp*, *meňzär*.

ex.en: Let's eat first, then we'll go.

cards.note: Means the same as *soň*, a little more formal.
p becomes b before a vowel. *Sebäbi* (its reason) is also the word for **because**.

ex.en: A strong wind is blowing today.

cards.note: *Yza* (back), *yzynda* (behind it), *yzyndan* (after it, following it).

ex.en: I go to bed at ten in the evening.

cards.note: *Ýatyr* (is lying) also builds a progressive after a verb in *-yp*: *uklap ýatyr* (is sleeping).
It takes the case the verb needs: *biri-birine kömek edýärler* (they help each other).

en: to marry, to get married (of a man)

ex.en: My brother got married last year.

cards.note: Said of a man; a woman *durmuşa çykýar*. Built on *öý* (house, home).

ex.en: There's a lot of traffic in the street.

cards.note: *Hereket etmek* (to move; to act).
Means the same as *hemişe*.

ex.en: Do you have any plans for tomorrow?

ex.tk: Adatça men işe awtobus bilen gidýärin.
ex.en: I usually go to work by bus.

en: number (of a phone, a room, a bus)
cards.note: The everyday word; official writing prefers *belgi*: *telefon belgisi*.

ex.en: My grandfather told us a story.
My dream is to become a doctor.

cards.note: *Arzuw etmek* (to wish).

ex.en: There are all kinds of fruit at the market.

cards.note: *Dürli-dürli* (all sorts of).

ex.en: That young man is my brother.

cards.note: t becomes d before a vowel: *ýigidi*.

ex.en: The shop is close to our house.

cards.note: What it's near takes the dative: *öýe ýakyn*. *Ýakyn dost* (a close friend).

ex.en: I have lunch with my colleagues.
There are two mistakes in this letter.

cards.note: k becomes g before a vowel: *ýalňyşlygy*. From *ýalňyş* (wrong).

ex.en: Everyone has their own job to do.
The lesson starts in five minutes.

cards.note: *Bäşinji* (fifth).

ex.tk: Men kesel, şu gün işe gitmeýärin.
ex.en: I'm ill, I'm not going to work today.

cards.note: *Kesel bolmak* (to fall ill).

ex.en: I had two eggs in the morning.
A famous writer wrote this book.

cards.note: *Ýazmak* (to write) with *-yjy*, like *satyjy* (seller).

ex.en: Magtymguly is a great Turkmen poet.

cards.note: *Goşgy* (poem).
One word for **foot** and **leg**. k becomes g before a vowel: *aýagym*.

en: to be useful, to do good

ex.en: This medicine will do you good.

cards.note: Who or what it's good for takes the dative: *saňa ýarar*.
To one person you call *sen*: *Hoş geldiň!*

ex.en: Do you have any information about this?
There are many passengers on the bus.
This shirt is a hundred manat.

cards.note: Not the noun *ýüz* (face): *Ýüzüňi ýuw* (Wash your face).
Opposite: *kyn* (difficult).
*Syýahat* (a trip, travel).

ex.tk: Bu film ýaşaýyş we ölüm barada.
ex.en: This film is about life and death.

cards.note: From *ölmek* (to die).

ex.en: Who's the owner of this shop?

ex.tk: Ýa sen gel, ýa men geleýin.
ex.en: Either you come or I'll come.

cards.note: *Ýa … ýa* (either … or). For a simple **or**, *ýa-da* is more usual.
With what falls: *ýagyş ýagýar* (it's raining), *gar ýagýar* (it's snowing).
*Satyjy* (seller). **To buy** is *satyn almak*.
